idiom_name: sealed interface + data classes with a children property
implementation_notes: Kotlin's sealed hierarchies are closed at compile time, so the classic base-class/visitor skeleton collapses into a sealed interface with a children property and one class per node kind; generic passes iterate children, and per-node dispatch is a when expression the compiler proves exhaustive without an else (verified: sealed subclasses are known at compile time). The data class modifiers supply equality and destructuring for node payload, replacing much of the classic boilerplate. A visitor interface is only worth adding when operations must live in a separate module from the node types.
pitfalls: data class equality and hashCode recurse through children, so comparing two large trees is O(tree) and can overflow the stack; plain classes or overridden equality avoid the surprise.
children built as a val list at construction allocates per node; fine for a parser, but a node rebuilt inside a hot loop pays it every time.
when exhaustiveness holds only for a sealed hierarchy in the same module/package: moving a subclass makes the check fail or forces an else that silently absorbs new cases.
